title: Why Can You See Your Breath When It's Cold? 🥶 #Shorts
description:
Why can you see your breath when it's cold? Your lungs are a damp place, so every breath out is warm and full of invisible water vapor. Outside, it hits cold air and loses heat fast. Once it cools to its dew point, some of that vapor turns into thousands of tiny water droplets: a very small, very temporary cloud. Real clouds and fog form the same way. A second later the droplets evaporate again. It doesn't have to be freezing either: on a humid morning you can see your breath in the 40s, and on a dry day you might not see it at all.

Explained in 60, podcast edition
